transcript.answer: At most three upkeep runs can start per repository for one event, such as a push to main. Since 2026-10-25 (FR12.19a), the pull requests go in order of how long ago they were last upkept, longest ago first. A pull request that has never been upkept goes first. Next comes the one whose newest upkeep run started earliest. Ties go to the oldest pull request. Before this change the three oldest pull requests always won. When those three kept failing, they took every start on every push, and the other loop pull requests were deferred indefinitely. Pull requests that don't get a start are left for the next event. Upkeep also skips pull requests that aren't behind main, and, since 2026-10-25, ones whose ticket is parked with lore:blocked.

judgements.reason: The answer states the cap of three per event per repository and the longest-ago-upkept ordering (never upkept first, then earliest newest upkeep run, then oldest), matching the gold; extra details do not contradict it.
